terms.gloss: go and see, meet (to speak with)
terms.grammar: verb, fourth conjugation; transitive, convenīre aliquem
evidence: Cic. Sen. 32: nēmō adhūc convenīre mē voluit, cui fuerim occupātus
Cic. Fam. 9.14.1: conveniō autem cotīdiē plūrimōs
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “to go to one to speak to him, make a request of him, etc., to address, accost, meet, visit”. Latin names the way one gets in touch: in person convenīre, by letter or email scrībere ad aliquem, by messenger nūntium mittere, by phone tēlephōnicē colloquī (see talk on the phone).

terms.gloss: write to someone (a letter, an email)
terms.grammar: scrībō, scrībere, scrīpsī, scrīptum, with ad and the accusative
evidence: Cic. Att. 6.1.26: ergō id ipsum scrībēs ad mē

terms.latin: per litterās aut per nūntium certiōrem facere
terms.gloss: let someone know by letter or by message
terms.grammar: certiōrem (certus), with faciō, facere, fēcī, factum; the person in the accusative
evidence: Cic. Att. 11.24.4: nē per litterās quidem aut per nūntium certiōrem facit mē

phrases.latin: Philotīmus nōn modo nūllus vēnit sed nē per litterās quidem aut per nūntium certiōrem facit mē quid ēgerit
phrases.english: Philotimus hasn’t come at all, and hasn’t even been in touch by letter or by messenger to tell me what he has done

phrases.latin: itaque nēmō adhūc convenīre mē voluit, cui fuerim occupātus
phrases.english: so far nobody who wanted to see me has found me busy

sources: Lewis & Short: convenio · Lewis & Short: scribo · Lewis & Short: certus
